source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.6 Line 8 ('a person is 65 years of age on the day before his 65th birthday')

worked: Federal AGI = wages (person 0) 40,000.00 = 40,000.00. Federal taxable income = 40,000.00 - 15,750.00 federal standard deduction - 1 x 2,000.00 age 65 additional = 22,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 5, Single. Start at federal AGI 40,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 40,000.00. Line 14 standard deduction 2,300.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 1; line 10 = 1 x 1,500.00 = 1,500.00; line 11 6,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 7,500.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 40,000.00 - 2,300.00 - 7,500.00 = 30,200.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 20,200.00 x 4.4% = 888.80; line 4 and line 17 = 888.80. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 888.80. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 889; expected keeps the formula result. Born January 1, 1961: 65 on December 31, 2025, the last day of the tax year, so the exemption applies.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.
